source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text:
Variety selection: the manual profiles named varieties tested/grown in Cambodia — DT84, MTD176, B3039, Chakkrabandhu No.1, and Asca — with a comparison table giving days to 100% flowering, days to physiological maturity, and days to harvest maturity for each; DT84 is noted as the earliest and most widely used variety in this list. A second table cross-references maturity windows against provinces (Battambang, Pailin, Kampong Cham) and planting-time recommendations by month for each.

Seed quality and viability: the manual stresses that seed vigour (germination percentage and seedling vigour) directly determines crop establishment and yield potential, with a graph showing yield rising with germination-test percentage (R² ≈ 0.36 in the cited trial), and recommends farmers conduct their own germination test before large-scale planting rather than assume purchased or saved seed is viable. Seed storage life is discussed — soybean seed loses viability faster than many other crop seeds, especially under Cambodia's hot, humid storage conditions, so farmers are advised to use fresh seed each season where possible and store any carried-over seed in cool, dry, pest-proof conditions.
